en: The Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī Sūtra,
translated by Du Xingyi of Jingzhao during the Great Tang Dynasty by Imperial Decree.
Homage to the All-Knowing One!
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park,
together with a great assembly of eight thousand bhikṣus.
There were thirty-two thousand bodhisattvas who had attained right wisdom and illuminated all phenomena;
regarding what is known and what is to be known, they were entirely free from obstruction.
Their names were: the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāyāna-prāpta,
the Bodhisattva Maitreya, the Youthful Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī,
the Bodhisattva Padma-śrīgarbha, and the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas such as Dharaṇīdhara,
Gaganagañja, Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, and Samantabhadra were the leaders;
such was the assembly of thirty-two thousand Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, there were ten thousand Brahmā-devas,
with Subhūti Brahmā as their leader,
who came from other realms of existence to the place where the Buddha was and assembled together in the gathering.

Furthermore, there were twelve thousand members of the Śakra-deva assembly who came together with immeasurable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others to attend the assembly.
At that time, the Holy One was surrounded by the fourfold assembly;
they paid him respectful homage and made offerings as he preached the Dharma.
At that moment, in the Sudharmā Hall of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, there was a deva named Susthita.
Dwelling in a magnificent palace of great jewels, they indulge in abundant pleasures;
attended by beautiful courtesans, they frolic and travel about,
observing sights that delight the mind and fully satisfy all their desires.
Suddenly, one night, a voice called out, "Tianshanzhu!
Your end has arrived; you shall die in seven days.
For seven lifetimes you shall be born in Jambudvīpa and enter hell."
Later, he was reborn as a poor man who was blind from birth and suffered various afflictions.
Upon hearing this, Sunetra became terrified and agitated; his hair stood on end and he was filled with sorrow.
He hurried to the abode of Śakra Devānām-indra, the Heavenly Lord.
Prostrating before the Lord’s feet, he spoke with wild trepidation,
entreating the Lord to show him compassion.
"Save me from this suffering and distress! Save me from this suffering and distress!
Having received celestial pleasures and indulged my heart to its content, suddenly a voice declares that my life will end in seven days."
Having been born seven times in Jambudvīpa, I shall enter hell.
Thereafter, I may be born as a human, but impoverished, blind from birth, and subject to all manner of suffering and affliction.
Now, my mind is weary and desolate, my thoughts are deluded and my consciousness disordered; I do not know how to find the way out.
"May Your Majesty take pity and deliver us from this bitter suffering.
Having heard these words, Śakra Devānām-indra was deeply moved by wonder and sorrow, wondering: "What does 'seven births' mean?"
After remaining silent for a brief moment, he then saw that Śānta,
having passed away from this life, had taken birth in the body of a pig;
once his existence as a pig ended, he received the body of a dog.
When the canine body has ended, he receives the body of a fox;
when the fox body has ended, he receives the body of a monkey;
when the monkey body has ended, he receives the body of a venomous snake.
When his existence as a snake has ended, he shall receive the body of a vulture;
when his existence as a vulture has ended, he shall receive the body of a crow.
Thus, for seven births, he will constantly consume filth and impurities.
When Śakra Devānām Indra saw this, he felt profound pity for Shan-zhu,
who was about to undergo great suffering; he pondered what plan to adopt,
from whom to seek help, and who might be able to rescue him.
Reflecting thus, he thought, "Except for the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, there is no one capable of saving me.
Then, during the latter part of that night, the Devendra—
Carrying various flower garlands, diverse kinds of incense— powdered incense and burning incense—
as well as celestial garments, necklaces, and various ornaments,
they went to the Jeta Grove to the presence of the Buddha, the Holy Honored One.
Having prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him seven times, and made extensive offerings,
he sat to one side before the Buddha and reported the matter of Suvihita in detail to the Holy One.
At that time, the Tathāgata emitted a great light from the crown of his head.
This light, of variegated colors, flowed forth and illuminated all realms of sentient beings throughout the ten directions;
it then returned to the Buddha’s presence, circled him three times to the right, and entered through the Buddha’s mouth.
The Buddha then smiled and addressed Śakra Devānām Indra:
"There is a Buddha-empowerment, pure for all realms of existence, the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī,
which completely purifies all karmic obstructions, hells, and animal births."
O Lord of Devas, this *Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī* purifies all realms of existence,
bringing an end to the suffering of birth and death in the Yama-loka and shattering the path to hell to ascend upon the Way of the Buddhas.
However, for those who merely hear it, all karmic obstructions that cause the continuity of birth and death,
as well as all manner of sufferings and afflictions, shall be completely extinguished;
they shall obtain good fruits and attain the knowledge of past lives.
They pass from one buddha-field to another buddha-field,
and from one heavenly realm to another heavenly realm;
even up to the palaces of the Trāyastriṃśa gods, they always know their past lives.
Those who are able to study and uphold it will live for a full hundred years and have their lifespan further increased; their body,
speech, and mind will be pure, and their hearts will be tranquil and at ease.
All physical suffering is eliminated and one attains all manner of wholesome sensations.
The Buddhas gaze upon them and the devas provide protection;
all Bodhisattvas regard them with loving-kindness and mindfulness.
For those who read and recite it, all hells, the animal realm,
the realm of Yama, and all hungry ghosts shall be stilled,
eliminated, and dispersed until their domains become empty and void.
The gates of merit were all opened in every Buddha-field and the celestial palaces of the bodhisattvas, leading them to enter. Thereupon,
Śakra Devānām Indra came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying, "O Holy Honored One,"
Out of compassion, you protect all sentient beings;
we pray that you will teach the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī*, which purifies all realms of existence.
At that time, the Holy Honored One accepted the request of the Lord of Devas.
Then he spoke the dhāraṇī, saying: Namo bhagavate tilukye pratisarāyai.

those marked as "heavy" (*guru*) are to be read with a guttural emphasis; those marked as "long" (*dīrgha*) are to be read with a prolonged vowel.)

Regarding the reversed characters, they are read according to the borrowed sounds of the reversed forms; for characters such as *la*, *li*, *lu*, *li*, *lei*, and *lan*, when a mouth radical is added to their side, they are read with a shifted tone.
This is the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī* of the Buddha’s Crown, which purifies all destinies of the gods and humans.
It purifies all karmic obstacles and eliminates all evil destinies;
it is proclaimed, protected, and joyfully praised by eight hundred and eighty-eight koṭis of hundreds of thousands of Ganges-sands of Buddhas.
It is sealed with the wisdom-seal of all Tathāgatas,
for the sake of eliminating all evil destinies:
all the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama.
For the sake of liberating those of various sinful natures who are submerged in the ocean of suffering and afflicted by manifold pains and poisons;
and for the sake of those with short lifespans, meager merit, and lowly appearance.
Because of sentient beings who, due to base and evil karma,
proceed toward the various classes of birth in the hells, meet with premature death, lose their minds,
and stray from the correct path; because of these sentient beings.
This dhāraṇī is taught to circulate throughout Jambudvīpa to purify karmic offenses and lead beings to liberation.
O Lord of Devas, you should uphold this Sovereign and Exalted Dhāraṇī and explain it to Suvikrāntavikrāmin.
For the sake of all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa, including the devas, sons of gods, and all conscious beings, you should proclaim,
recite, contemplate, study, and keep this in mind;
you should honor it with offerings, uphold it, and practice it.
I now instruct and entrust you, Lord of Devas, with this dhāraṇī seal;
you should uphold it well. Those who hear this dhāraṇī shall [be purified] throughout hundreds of thousands of kalpas.
All accumulated karmic obstructions shall be completely purified;
one shall not fall into hell, nor be born as an animal,
nor enter the evil destinies of the Yama-loka or hungry ghosts.
One does not receive the bodies of asuras,
yakṣas, rākṣasas, pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas, those afflicted by madness, and other such spirits; nor even those of dogs,
tortoises, birds, beasts, mosquitoes, gadflies, venomous snakes, or crawling reptiles.
Along with all small insects, they shall no longer undergo rebirth;
they will always be in the company of the Buddha, or be born into the superior clans of Bodhisattvas,
or into great Brahmin lineages, great Kṣatriya lineages, or great households of householders.
By the power of this dhāraṇī, one attains birth in purity and reaches the seat of enlightenment to achieve perfect, universal awakening.
O Lord of Devas, this is the dhāraṇī for the supreme excellence of all pure realms.
His majestic spiritual power is vast, endowed with great meritorious fruits;
he possesses great strength and capability, a source of supreme auspiciousness.
Like a *sūryagarbha* jewel, he is brilliant and stainless, pure as the sky.
Wherever it is located, it will be illuminated with brilliant light;
wherever this dhāraṇī is placed, its majestic spiritual power will likewise pervade that place in the same manner.
One who upholds this dhāraṇī cannot be defiled by any evil deeds;
they become gentle, supple, pure, and stainless, like Jāmbūnada gold.
One who copies, reads, studies, recites, contemplates, makes offerings to,
upholds, and practices this dhāraṇī should know that the karma of the hells in that place will be eliminated and all realms of existence will be purified.
Write this dhāraṇī and place it atop a banner,
erected upon a high mountain, a high roof,
or other elevated places, or within a stūpa.
If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or sons and daughters of good family behold this dhāraṇī-banner,
or if they come near the banner, or if the shadow of the banner falls upon their bodies, or if the wind from the banner blows against them.
Or, if dust from a wind-blown banner should strike their bodies,
their karmic offenses will be extinguished,
and they shall not be reborn among the denizens of hell, animals, the realm of Yama, hungry ghosts, or asuras.
They shall not fall into any of the evil realms; all Tathāgatas and Buddhas shall bestow upon them the prediction of enlightenment (vyākaraṇa).
They shall attain non-retrogression and ascend to perfect awakening.
With various flowers and incense...
With various kinds of garlands, various banners and parasols,
pennants, canopies, necklaces, and all manner of ornaments,
as well as various ointments and decorations, they performed great offerings.
One should construct a stūpa at a crossroads,
install this dhāraṇī therein, and practice the path by prostrating;
you should know that such persons are mahāsattvas.
The Dharma-son of the Buddha, the pillar of the Dharma, the stūpa of the śarīra.
At that time, Yama, the King of Dharma,
came to the place where the Buddha was as the night was turning to dawn.
With various celestial flowers, various incenses, blended perfumes,
burning incense, celestial robes, and necklaces,
they performed great offerings and circumambulated [the object] seven times to the right.
Prostrating at the Buddha’s feet, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O Holy One, I know the Buddha’s kindness; it is not that I am ungrateful.
Now, in order to repay the Buddha’s kindness, I shall protect all beings."
"One should always diligently serve this dhāraṇī of great majesty and great efficacy,
which closes the gates of hell and purifies all evil realms.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings circumambulated the Buddha three times and addressed him, saying:
"I only pray that the Holy One will explain the method for practicing this dhāraṇī.
The Buddha told the Four Heavenly Kings, "Listen attentively, listen attentively; I shall now speak.
If there are those with short lifespans who seek long life..."
On the fifteenth day of the waxing moon,
having bathed to become pure and donned clean garments,
one should observe the eightfold precepts and recite this dhāraṇī one thousand times.
All obstacles shall be removed, illnesses cured, and lifespan increased, so that they attain great peace and happiness.
They shall be completely liberated from the sufferings of the hells, the animal realm, and all evil destinies,
even including those among the various species of the animal realm and other evil destinies.
Those who hear this dhāraṇī with their ears shall no longer receive bodies in the evil realms;
those afflicted by grave illnesses shall have all their ailments dispelled, and all realms of existence shall become pure.
After the end of their lives, they will be born in the realm of manifest bliss;
they will be born by transformation from a lotus, not from a womb, and will always know their past lives.
Yet, if sentient beings are led away by the power of their own sinful karma, [they will not attain this].
After their life ends, they will be reborn in the evil realms.
One should take this dhāraṇī and recite it twenty-one times over soil, which is then scattered upon their skeletal remains;
wherever they may be reborn—whether in hell or as an animal—the [soil] shall follow them there.
Whether they were in the realm of Yama, the world of hungry ghosts,
or even in the Avīci Hell, among birds, beasts, or insects,
all were relieved of their suffering bodies and reborn in heaven to enjoy bliss.
If one recites this dhāraṇī twenty-one times every day, their transgressions will be extinguished,
their merit will increase, and they will be loved and respected by all people.
After the end of their life, they will be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
If one constantly recites and maintains this dhāraṇī,
after the end of life, one will be reborn in the various pure lands,
proceeding from one Buddha-field to another Buddha-field.
They shall emit great light throughout all Buddha-fields;
they shall always be in the company of the Buddhas, protected and nurtured by them, and receive their prediction of enlightenment,
until finally attaining the bliss of Great Nirvana.
One who practices this dhāraṇī should construct a square altar, perfectly equal on all four sides,
scattering various kinds of pure flowers and burning various kinds of incense.
Placing the right knee-wheel on the ground and kneeling with single-mindedness,
one should universally bring to mind all Buddhas of the ten directions;
forming the mudrā of the joined ten fingers and toes, one should hold it at the heart.
Bend the two index fingers and the two thumbs so that they press against one another.
Recite "Sādhu" (Excellent!), and chant this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times.
This shall constitute making offerings and serving eighty-eight koṭis of Ganges-sand *nayutas* of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.
One makes offerings as if making offerings to the Buddha;
one also makes offerings to the Four Great Heavenly Kings.
All praise them as virtuous and call them children of the Buddha.
Adorning their minds with great bodhi, they attain unimpeded wisdom.
Anyone who wishes to recite this dhāraṇī should, with a sincere mind,
perform the ritual according to the Dharma by forming the mudrā of the ten fingers joined together.
This is the practice of the dharani method.
The Buddha told Śakra Devānām Indra:
"O Heavenly Lord, you should use this method to rescue and deliver sentient beings."
All the sufferings of the hells and all realms of existence shall be purified;
the karma of those realms shall be cleansed, and the fruit of long life shall be obtained.
O Lord of Devas, you should now return and bestow this dhāraṇī upon the Devaputra Susthitamati.
"When seven days have passed, you and Suṣṭhita shall come to my place.
Having received the Buddha’s instruction, Śakra Devānām Indra returned to his celestial palace with this Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī.
It was bestowed upon the Devaputra Susthita.
Having received it, Susthita practiced and made offerings for six days and six nights.
Upon reaching the seventh day, he attained liberation from all karmic actions leading to the evil realms.
Dwelling in the realm of celestial bliss, they obtain great longevity.
With joy and exultation, they cry out in a loud voice:
"Adho Buddhāya! Adho Dharmāya! Adho Saṃghāya! Adho Vidyādhara-dhāraṇī! Savior of all sentient beings from every suffering and calamity!"
"May I be liberated from the sufferings of the evil realms.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, surrounded by his retinue and attendants,
took the prince Sudhīra and brought various kinds of flowers and incense.
Incense, ointments, and various kinds of garlands;
parasols, canopies, banners, flags, robes, and necklaces;
they mounted celestial jeweled chariots, fully equipped with heavenly ornaments.
Having arrived at where the Buddha was, he made a great offering, circumambulated him ten thousand times,
and then stood to one side before the Buddha.
After praising the Buddha in verse, he withdrew to sit and listen to the Dharma.
The Buddha extended his golden right hand,
comforted and protected Śubhavyūha, and bestowed upon him a prophecy of enlightenment.
*The Sutra of the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī*.
